rationale: The revised proposition faithfully states the constant-coefficient homogeneous first-order system in equation (1.1). Its two derivative witnesses are tied to the correct coordinate slices, A is fixed and real, matrix-vector multiplication acts only on q_x, and the equality is to the pointwise zero vector. The proof-carrying binder is not a hidden applicability restriction: ConstantCoefficientLinearSystemSolution consists of exactly a state q and a proof of the same pointwise predicate for all x,t, while its constructor packages every q with such a proof. Hence unpacking and repackaging establish both implication directions, and the theorem does not assert source-absent existence or uniqueness. The hypotheses are nonvacuous: for m > 0 and any A, affine states q(x,t) = x v - t(A v) satisfy the equation, and constant states do as well. Lean also admits m = 0; this is an empty, fully defined, trivial coordinate case that the source does not discuss, but it neither weakens any intended case nor constitutes genuine nonvacuous extra strength. No dependency or semantic check remains unresolved, so adjudication is not required.
